input.reflection: Log evidence: ts-travel-plan-service emits 1447 SEVERE 'Request processing failed; nested exception is java.lang.NullPointerException' — exactly matching the 1447 HTTP 500 on /travelPlan/quickest. Logs are within a ~4 minute window (2025-07-23 21:29–21:33). The NPE occurs ~13ms into request after getByQuickest, with no downstream child spans, so the fault is in travel-plan's own code path (not a dependency). Still to check: (a) normal-baseline quickest behavior, (b) whether ui-dashboard quickest 200s (17, avg 1.5s) are slow due to retries, (c) resource metrics on travel-plan pods / route-plan OPTIONS anomaly, (d) whether another fault exists (ui-dashboard login 106ms, food-service AMQP errors, route-plan POST latency). The AMQP errors in delivery/notification look like a separate, lower-volume side issue (RabbitMQ connectivity).

input.reflection: Quickest comparison: normal baseline quickest flow is ui-dashboard -> travel-plan (636ms) -> route-plan quickestRoute (419ms), 200 OK. Abnormal: travel-plan quickest throws NPE at ~13ms before any downstream call, so route-plan quickestRoute is never invoked (route-plan shows only OPTIONS preflights 1447, which is a side effect of the failing calls, not a fault). Resource metrics are mostly flat; travel-plan CPU rose (0.257 vs 0.088) consistent with error-path load, not a saturation root cause. Remaining check: are AMQP (delivery/notification/food->MQ) errors and food-service errors present in normal? If they're absent in normal, they're a possible second fault (RabbitMQ connectivity) — but they are low-volume and not on the user-facing latency path to the degraded endpoints.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, level, left(message,90) msg, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs WHERE message ILIKE '%AMQP%' OR message ILIKE '%queue%' OR message ILIKE '%Get the Get Food%' OR message ILIKE '%ConnectException%' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, level, left(message,90), count(*) FROM normal_logs WHERE message ILIKE '%AMQP%' OR message ILIKE '%queue%' OR message ILIKE '%Get the Get Food%' OR message ILIKE '%ConnectException%' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC

SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,1) avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) e5 FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name LIKE 'POST /api/v1/travelplanservice%' OR span_name LIKE 'GET /api/v1/foodservice%' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,1), sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM normal_traces WHERE span_name LIKE 'POST /api/v1/travelplanservice%' OR span_name LIKE 'GET /api/v1/foodservice%' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY service_name, src

content.text:
## Investigation summary

**Bottom line:** One root cause. `ts-travel-plan-service` throws a `NullPointerException` on its `POST /api/v1/travelplanservice/travelPlan/quickest` handler, so every quickest-search request fails with HTTP 500. `ts-ui-dashboard` surfaces this to users as 5xx errors and slow responses.

### Affected endpoints and services

| Service / endpoint | Abnormal | Normal baseline | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ts-travel-plan-service` `POST /travelPlan/quickest` | 1,447 × HTTP 500, ~13 ms | 0 errors, ~637 ms avg (success) | Primary fault |
| `ts-ui-dashboard` `POST /travelPlan/quickest` | 82 × 500 (avg 3.4 s), 17 × 200 (avg 1.5 s) | 62 × 200, ~639 ms | User-facing symptom |
| `ts-ui-dashboard` (all routes) | 83 × 5xx, p95 786 ms | 0 × 5xx, p95 218 ms | Downstream propagation |
| `ts-route-plan-service` `quickestRoute` | Never called on the failing path | 62 calls, ~419 ms | Not faulty; simply not reached |

Errors are confined to the quickest search. The `minStation` and `cheapest` travel-plan paths returned 200 in the abnormal window.

### Evidence for the root cause
- **Logs:** `ts-travel-plan-service` emits 1,447 SEVERE entries, "Request processing failed; nested exception is java.lang.NullPointerException". The count matches the 500s exactly. The normal window has none.
- **Traces:** Failing spans are `TravelPlanController.getByQuickest` (~7 ms) with no downstream child spans. The request dies in the service's own code before calling route-plan. In the normal baseline, the same path calls `ts-route-plan-service` `quickestRoute` and succeeds.
- **Timeline:** Errors begin at 21:29 and peak at 21:31–21:32 (about 400 travel-plan 500s per minute), in step with the load pattern.

### Ruled out
- **RabbitMQ / AMQP errors** in `ts-delivery-service` and `ts-notification-service` (48 each) and `ts-food-service` errors appear at similar levels in the normal logs. They are baseline noise.
- **Route-plan OPTIONS spans** (1,447) are a side effect of the failing calls, not a separate fault.
- **Resource saturation:** Memory and filesystem metrics are essentially flat versus normal. `ts-travel-plan-service` CPU is higher (0.257 vs 0.088), which fits error-path work rather than being a cause.

### Propagation
`ts-travel-plan-service` (NPE in quickest handler) → `ts-ui-dashboard` (500s and added latency on `/travelPlan/quickest`) → end users (the support ticket).

### Caveats
- Travel-plan records 1,447 failing quickest spans, but ui-dashboard records only about 99 quickest spans. Either the gateway traces are partially sampled or some callers bypass the gateway. The direction of causality is unaffected, but the exact user-facing failure count may be understated.
- The exception stack trace is truncated in the logs, so the precise NPE site in the code is not confirmed. A code-level check of the quickest handler is the next step.
